extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit newsrooms considering INN membership; INN members and stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards used by the Institute for Nonprofit News (INN) to evaluate organizations applying for membership, including eligibility, editorial standards, independence, transparency, and membership-category expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational eligibility (nonprofit & primary mission)
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization must be organized as a nonprofit and have as its primary mission news reporting in order to be eligible for INN membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a threshold requirement; applicants that are not nonprofit-organized or whose primary mission is not news reporting are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary standards: editorial excellence, editorial independence, financial transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: INN’s criteria for membership is centered on three primary standards: editorial excellence in news coverage, editorial independence and financial transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three standards are the core lens through which applications are evaluated; nuances are interpreted by staff, the Standards Task Force, and ultimately the board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial quality — original news reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The newsroom must conduct original news reporting; full members 'regularly publish original investigative or public service journalism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of original reporting is a common reason for decline (example: an applicant mostly republished content and was recommended for decline). Provisionally accepted organizations are expected to increase original reporting to meet standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial quality — opinion labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Opinion pieces must be labeled appropriately so audiences can distinguish opinion from news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insufficient labeling of opinion content can result in deferral or request for improvements (example: one applicant was deferred because it needed better labeling on its opinion pieces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial quality — distinguish advertising from news
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsrooms must clearly distinguish advertising from news content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to separate advertising and editorial content undermines editorial quality expectations and can affect membership decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence — no advocacy or undue influence
rubrics_metrics.description: INN members must be independent from advocacy and financial or other influence, ensuring coverage serves no cause beyond informing the public and communities served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants have been declined for asking readers to take actions to further a specific movement; outlets may provide resources or inform about events (polling places, protests) but cannot tell people who to vote for or what policies to support. Publications explicitly 'by and for' a specific group (e.g., religious publications abiding by shared doctrine) may be judged insufficiently independent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial transparency — donor disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations are required to publicly name contributions of $5,000 or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables the public to know financial supporters; lack of adequate disclosure can jeopardize membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial transparency — leadership and policy disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: INN members must make it easy for the public to identify board members and key leaders, as well as operational and ethical policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly accessible information about leadership and policies is part of the transparency standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full member expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Full members regularly publish original investigative or public service journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the practical expectation for full membership as distinct from provisional or affiliate categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional member requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional members receive support while working to fully meet INN’s membership standards for editorial excellence, independence and transparency within a year of acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional members are often fiscally sponsored while launching fundraising efforts and can access peer support; note that INN is not accepting applications for provisional members after Dec. 31, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliate membership criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliate membership is open to organizations that share INN’s mission but aren’t primarily newsrooms; affiliates are not eligible for INN philanthropic programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliates should align with INN’s mission but are explicitly excluded from certain member benefits tied to being a primary newsroom; INN is not accepting affiliate applications after Dec. 31, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application review process and decision authority
rubrics_metrics.description: INN staff reviews each application and makes a recommendation to the board (approve, decline, or defer); the board makes the final decision. When staff are unsure, they engage the Standards Task Force for interpretation and consistent application of standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are considered across three cycles; staff may approve some without Task Force input, while ambiguous or complex cases are elevated. The Task Force includes co-founders and long-term members to help interpret standards amid field growth and complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral/decline process and remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: When an organization is declined or deferred, INN staff sends an email explaining the decision and offers an option to schedule a meeting and receive feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decline is often the start of a conversation; INN offers feedback on what could help an organization successfully reapply. Being declined makes future review more scrutinized but acceptance after a prior decline does occur.
